Common Survival Simulation Results

Source: R/class_simulation_results.R
SimulationResultsBaseSurvival.Rd

Base class for survival simulation results. Obtain specialized instances with getSimulationSurvival(), getSimulationMultiArmSurvival(), or getSimulationEnrichmentSurvival().

Details

Patient-wise dropout summaries use each arm or population's last contributing analysis, including discontinued groups. Replication proportions and finishing horizons are averaged over the same nonempty enrolled-subject denominators. Test-statistic-based simulations leave these fields unavailable.

Fields

maxNumberOfIterations

The number of simulation iterations. Is a single numeric value representing a whole number.

seed

The seed used for random number generation. Is a single numeric value.

allocationRatioPlanned

The planned allocation ratio (n1 / n2) for the groups. For multi-arm designs, it is the allocation ratio relating the active arm(s) to the control. Is a single positive numeric value.

conditionalPower

The conditional power at each stage of the trial. Is a single numeric value between 0 and 1.

iterations

The number of iterations used for simulations. Is a single numeric value representing a whole number.

futilityPerStage

The per-stage probabilities of stopping the trial for futility. Is a numeric matrix.

futilityStop

In simulation results data set: indicates whether trial is stopped for futility or not.

calcEventsFunction

An optional function that can be entered to define how event size is recalculated. By default, recalculation is performed with conditional power with specified minNumberOfEventsPerStage and maxNumberOfEventsPerStage.

directionUpper

Specifies the direction of the alternative, only applicable for one-sided testing. Default is TRUE which means that larger values of the test statistics yield smaller p-values. Is a single logical value.

expectedNumberOfEvents

The expected number of events under specified alternative. Is a numeric vector.

maxNumberOfEventsPerStage

Determines the maximum number of events per stage for data-driven sample size recalculation. Is a numeric vector of length kMax containing whole numbers.

minNumberOfEventsPerStage

Determines the minimum number of events per stage for data-driven sample size recalculation. Is a numeric vector of length kMax containing whole numbers.

plannedEvents

Determines the number of cumulated (overall) events in survival designs when the interim stages are planned. For two treatment arms, is the number of events for both treatment arms. For multi-arm designs, refers to the overall number of events for the selected arms plus control. Is a numeric vector of length kMax containing whole numbers.

thetaH0

The difference or assumed effect under H0. Is a single numeric value.

thetaH1

The assumed effect under the alternative hypothesis. For survival designs, refers to the hazard ratio. Is a numeric vector.

studyDuration

The study duration for specified effect size. Is a positive numeric vector.

maxStudyDuration

The maximum study duration in survival designs. Is a numeric vector.

observedDropoutProportion1

Mean replication-specific observed dropout proportion in arm 1, counting dropout before the event and by the arm or population's last contributing analysis. Only replications with a finite finishing horizon and positive enrolled-subject denominator contribute; NA if none contribute. Available only for patient-wise simulation. Numeric vector over scenarios for two-arm trials; in multi-arm trials, arm 1 is a matrix of active-arm rows and scenario columns (a vector for one active arm), and arm 2 is a vector over scenarios for shared control. In enrichment trials, both arms have population rows (subpopulations followed by the full population) and scenario columns, or a vector for one population. Discontinued arms and populations are retained; overlapping populations include their shared subjects. There is no stage dimension. NULL for test-statistic-based simulation.

observedDropoutProportion2

Mean replication-specific observed dropout proportion in arm 2, counting dropout before the event and by the arm or population's last contributing analysis. Only replications with a finite finishing horizon and positive enrolled-subject denominator contribute; NA if none contribute. Available only for patient-wise simulation. Numeric vector over scenarios for two-arm trials; in multi-arm trials, arm 1 is a matrix of active-arm rows and scenario columns (a vector for one active arm), and arm 2 is a vector over scenarios for shared control. In enrichment trials, both arms have population rows (subpopulations followed by the full population) and scenario columns, or a vector for one population. Discontinued arms and populations are retained; overlapping populations include their shared subjects. There is no stage dimension. NULL for test-statistic-based simulation.

dropoutObservationTime1

Mean finishing analysis time in arm 1 over exactly the replications contributing to the corresponding observed dropout proportion, in the same time units as accrual and survival. NA if no replication contributes. Available only for patient-wise simulation. Numeric vector over scenarios for two-arm trials; in multi-arm trials, arm 1 is a matrix of active-arm rows and scenario columns (a vector for one active arm), and arm 2 is a vector over scenarios for shared control. In enrichment trials, both arms have population rows (subpopulations followed by the full population) and scenario columns, or a vector for one population. Discontinued arms and populations are retained; overlapping populations include their shared subjects. There is no stage dimension. NULL for test-statistic-based simulation.

dropoutObservationTime2

Mean finishing analysis time in arm 2 over exactly the replications contributing to the corresponding observed dropout proportion, in the same time units as accrual and survival. NA if no replication contributes. Available only for patient-wise simulation. Numeric vector over scenarios for two-arm trials; in multi-arm trials, arm 1 is a matrix of active-arm rows and scenario columns (a vector for one active arm), and arm 2 is a vector over scenarios for shared control. In enrichment trials, both arms have population rows (subpopulations followed by the full population) and scenario columns, or a vector for one population. Discontinued arms and populations are retained; overlapping populations include their shared subjects. There is no stage dimension. NULL for test-statistic-based simulation.
